cases.split: 600 gate (seen-error, checksum generator, verification flags, crc zero/nonzero, priorities 0..4, tracer selection, perf level 0..5, sync point, small data 0..64 B) + 600 growth (alignment 512/4096, capacity/cursize/max combinations pinning the doubling loop, the max cap and the direct-io max arm) + 600 write_paths (buffered/direct x verification x crc x remaining/left x Flush/WriteBuffered scripted outcomes x rate limiter x listeners, incl. the RangeSync arm with filesize > 1 MiB) + 600 bindings (body/source hashes, 40 caller-census sites, vtable slots 12/16/24, 29 writer-layout offsets, IOOptions defaults, 25-cell priority matrix, CRC vectors incl. check vector '123456789' -> 0xE3069283, Combine identities, AlignedBuffer unit rows, timer-guard thresholds, file-selection matrix)
what_is_checked: gate: seen_error returns code 5 with the 27-byte heap state_ and writes nothing; empty append sets pending_sync_ and advances nothing; filesize_ advances by data.size() on ok; checksum_generator_ records the UpdateFileChecksum call

growth: no growth when it fits; capacity doubles (4096 -> 8192 for a 5000 B write); growth stops at max (no desired size satisfies the loop for a 20000 B write with max 8192, so capacity stays 4096); the direct-io max arm grows to max even when the grown buffer still cannot hold the write; the AllocateNewBuffer skip guard (copy_data and desired<cursize) is pinned directly because the growth loop can never request it

write_paths: a buffered append stays in buf_ and Flush moves it to the file; the verification single append Combines (not Extends) the checksum; crc==0 takes the plain arm but the plain arm still Extends when both flags are set; the direct-io loop appends 4096 B, Extends, Flushes positionally, and leaves the 904 B tail buffered (Flush pads it to the 4096 B page, so the physical file is 8192 B); a Flush write failure sets seen_error_; a WriteBuffered failure clears the buffer and sets seen_error_; the RangeSync arm fires with filesize > 1 MiB and bytes_per_sync; a plain direct write bypasses the buffer entirely

bindings: both body hashes match the binary; the .cold source hash is reproduced by zeroing the 8 recorded relocations; the main function has no census record; the 39 call sites and 1 jump site are pinned; vtable slots 12/16/24; the 29 writer-layout offsets; IOOptions defaults (0x58 B image, type 7, rate_limiter_priority at +0x0c); the 25-cell DecideRateLimiterPriority matrix; CRC check vector, Combine == Value(a+b), degenerate Combine len2==0 == crc1^crc2, Mask/Unmask round-trip; timer guard armed iff perf_level > 2; file selection raw vs wrapper

observations: The seen-error gate is the first thing the body does: byte this+0x89 set -> IOStatus code 5 with the 27-byte heap state_ 'Writer has previous error.' (rodata 0x451480 'Writer has previ' + 0x452bf0 ' previous error.'), the old sret state_ delete[]'d first, and nothing else touched. Upstream writable_file_writer.h:555-563 (AssertFalseAndGetStatusForPrevError) returns exactly IOStatus::IOError("Writer has previous error.").

The single-append verification arm uses Crc32cCombine, NOT Extend: buffered_data_crc32c_checksum_ = Combine(old, crc, left). The direct-io loop arm uses Extend per chunk. The plain arm Extends too. So the same crc argument is folded three different ways depending on the arm -- pinned by the gate/write_paths cases.

The degenerate Combine len2==0 case (crc1^crc2) is live here: appending 0 bytes with verification on still changes buffered_data_crc32c_checksum_ to old^crc, because the binary calls Combine unconditionally with length=left.

The growth loop can never trigger the AllocateNewBuffer skip guard from Append: desired >= cap >= capacity >= cursize, so desired < cursize is unreachable. The guard is pinned by direct AlignedBuffer unit rows instead.
The CPU-timer half of the IOSTATS_TIMER_GUARD is dead: the flag (rsp+0x41), id (rsp+0x44) and object (rsp+0x60) are zeroed and never set. Only the wall-clock half runs, and only when perf_level > 2.

GetIOPriority is devirtualized by a vtable-address comparison: the guard compares slot 16 against the RELATIVE reloc at 0x64ecf30 (addend 0x5df6e90, the base implementation 'mov 0x18(%rdi),%eax; ret'). When equal, the binary reads file+0x18 directly; otherwise it makes the virtual call at 0x6054e90.
WriteDirect pads to the page boundary: flushing a 904 B buffered tail with direct I/O writes 4096 B positionally, so the physical file is 8192 B for 5000 logical bytes. Pinned by the direct-io test.

The .cold FDE is entered from six endbr64 stubs at the main FDE tail (0x6055143..0x605518b); only the jump at 0x605514a is the census-validated site. The stubs are part of the main FDE, not separate functions.

The IOOptions property_bag is built empty with a self-pointer bucket: the binary stores rsp+0xb8 at rsp+0xb8 itself (bucket count 1, max_load 1.0f) and destroys it via the _Hashtable dtor at 0x5d36110 after PrepareWrite.
unknowns: WriteBuffered, WriteBufferedWithChecksum, Flush and UpdateFileChecksum are taken as oracles here (their bodies are separate FDEs: Flush 0x6051a20 is census-bound, the others have no census record). Their internal steps are modelled from upstream source, not from their own binary bodies; reconstructing them is the natural follow-up.

Whether the returned status's bytes 6-7 (padding, never written by the Append callee's error path) ever matter to a caller: the 39 callers move the 16-byte status in their frames right after the call; whether bytes 6-7 are read was not traced.
The exact .cold entry-point selection (which exception region uses which of the six stubs at 0x6055143..0x605518b): the stubs and the pad are pinned, but the LSDA region mapping was not decoded.
